nodes.label: What a data pipeline test actually needs (blog post)

nodes.label: Run checks at the write boundary
nodes.norm_label: run checks at the write boundary
nodes.rationale: Three five-line checks instead of a full data-quality framework, run right before writing to a shared table, where failure is cheapest because nothing downstream has consumed bad data yet.

nodes.label: Null-rate check
nodes.rationale: Flags a normally well-populated column whose fill rate suddenly drops.

nodes.label: Row-count sanity check
nodes.rationale: Today's row count compared to trailing 7-day average.

nodes.label: Schema check
nodes.rationale: Depended-on columns exist with the expected type; catches input data shifting shape silently.

nodes.label: Tested pipeline framework with schema checks and staging
nodes.norm_label: tested pipeline framework with schema checks and staging
nodes.rationale: Notebook pipelines let a bad join silently corrupt reports for weeks; schema checks, a local test runner and a production-sized staging environment let analysts verify before merging, reducing review time and incidents.

nodes.label: Idempotent replayable settlement on Kafka with dead-letter queue
nodes.norm_label: idempotent replayable settlement on kafka with dead-letter queue
nodes.rationale: A nightly batch meant any failure required a full manual rerun; idempotent replayable steps, a DLQ for rows needing a human, and per-stage instrumentation removed duplicate payments and scaled to 3x volume without a rewrite.

nodes.label: Canary Deploy
nodes.rationale: Route a small slice of traffic (5%) to the new version and compare metrics against stable before promoting or rolling back, limiting blast radius of a bad release.

nodes.label: Canary deploys that roll back themselves (blog post)
nodes.norm_label: canary deploys that roll back themselves (blog post)

nodes.label: Northwind Labs - Senior Engineer, Platform & AI
nodes.norm_label: northwind labs - senior engineer, platform & ai

nodes.label: Automatic canary rollback with Slack report
nodes.norm_label: automatic canary rollback with slack report
nodes.rationale: A bad deploy costs five minutes of canary traffic instead of an incident, so the team ships smaller changes more often; no human decision needed at 6am.

nodes.label: Canary error-budget check
nodes.rationale: Compare canary error rate (<=1.5x baseline) and p99 latency (<=1.2x baseline) after a warm-up window so the promote/rollback decision is automatic instead of someone watching a dashboard.

nodes.label: GitHub Actions canary release pipeline with automatic rollback
nodes.norm_label: github actions canary release pipeline with automatic rollback
nodes.rationale: Replaced a spreadsheet/Slack/6am manual release with test suite, canary deploy, 15-minute error-rate watch, then promotion or automatic rollback when the error budget is exceeded; release time went from a day to 20 minutes.

nodes.label: Deploy workflow: build job
nodes.rationale: Runs npm ci, npm run build, npm test on Node 22 for every push/PR; uploads ./dist as a Pages artifact only on push to main.

nodes.label: Deploy workflow: deploy job (actions/deploy-pages)
nodes.rationale: Gated on main push and needs build, so a failing build never publishes and the last good site stays live.

nodes.label: Hashed CSP meta via Astro security.csp
nodes.norm_label: hashed csp meta via astro security.csp
nodes.rationale: GitHub Pages can't send real HTTP headers.

nodes.label: Astro static framework choice (v1)
nodes.rationale: Static by default, 0 KB JS unless opted in, native MDX, Zod content collections; no React because each interactive feature is under 50 lines of vanilla TS and React would add ~45 KB.

nodes.label: Meta http-equiv Content-Security-Policy
nodes.rationale: GitHub Pages cannot set HTTP headers, so CSP goes in a meta tag.

nodes.label: Framework and host comparison (Astro vs Eleventy/Hugo/Jekyll/Next.js; GitHub Pages vs Cloudflare/Netlify/Vercel)
nodes.norm_label: framework and host comparison (astro vs eleventy/hugo/jekyll/next.js; github pages vs cloudflare/netlify/vercel)
nodes.rationale: Astro chosen for typed Zod schemas, zero JS default, MDX and Fonts API; Eleventy runner-up lacks schemas. GitHub Pages chosen to keep code, content and host in one repo; Cloudflare's 2026 acquisition of Astro judged low risk since output is plain static files.

nodes.label: Grounding an assistant in docs that change weekly (blog post)
nodes.norm_label: grounding an assistant in docs that change weekly (blog post)

nodes.label: Always show the source
nodes.rationale: Linking every answer to its source page built more trust than prompt tweaks and lets support agents catch wrong or outdated docs immediately.

nodes.label: Re-index on write (webhook re-embed)
nodes.rationale: A stale index answers confidently with last month's process; re-embedding a page on wiki save instead of a nightly job cut index lag from up to 24h to seconds.
